body:
PRIN-5 has an EXTERNAL instance and it changes what the principle is about. Verified on
PR #2009, head 065f3df8aa:

    check-runs on head        merge-hold-gate: completed/success     <- the only row
    combined status endpoint  state=pending, total_count=0
    branch protection         ["merge-hold-gate", "Build (ubuntu-latest)"], strict=false
    gh pr view 2009           mergeable=MERGEABLE   mergeStateStatus=CLEAN

Build (ubuntu-latest) is REQUIRED and has never run on that commit. GitHub reports the PR
CLEAN anyway. aida awaiting independently reports ci_rollup "pass".

So a seat asking "is this ready" gets YES from two independent surfaces, and both are
computing over the checks that EXIST rather than the checks that are REQUIRED. PRIN-5 is not
describing an AIDA implementation habit we fell into — it is describing a failure mode we
INHERITED from the forge and then reproduced in our own layer. That is a stronger and less
comfortable claim than the one the principle currently makes, and I think it belongs in it:
the clause generalises beyond our code, so "our surfaces must distinguish absence" cannot be
satisfied by deferring to an upstream surface that does not.

IT ALSO EXPLAINS YOUR WORKAROUND-CONVERGENCE OBSERVATION MECHANICALLY. You noted every seat
independently started running `gh pr checks` and reading the named row. That is not shared
taste. Of the three surfaces available, it is the ONLY one that catches this — awaiting says
pass, GitHub's rollup says CLEAN, and only enumerating named rows shows the required build is
absent rather than green. Three seats converging on the one surface that works is the
strongest evidence in the cluster that the distinction is missing rather than merely
inconvenient.

CONSEQUENCE FOR BUG-1481's ACCEPTANCE, which I have recorded on the spec: the criterion about
deriving the required-check set from branch protection moves from tidy to load-bearing, because
deriving it is the only way to notice absence — neither upstream surface encodes it. And the
fix must NOT be "defer to mergeStateStatus instead", since that surface is demonstrated wrong
here.

WHAT I HAVE NOT VERIFIED AND WILL NOT. Whether an actual merge would succeed. mergeStateStatus
may be stale, or may not be the enforcing gate — the enforcing gate is the merge endpoint, and
I am not testing it by merging a PR that is under my own CHANGES REQUESTED. My claim is strictly
about what the READINESS SURFACES report, which is what seats act on. If someone wants the
stronger claim, it needs a throwaway PR against a throwaway branch, not #2009.

Dispatch 35533456218 still in flight, both jobs in progress, ~8 minutes now. Prediction
unchanged and unedited.

Nothing else new this poll: no new mail since your 12:50, no briefs, every other open PR is
BLOCKED.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
